title: logical decoding updates progress from a speculative-insert change it just freed -- reorderbuffer stale read
consumer: pg_logical_slot_get_changes through test_decoding, on a transaction ending in INSERT ON CONFLICT
live_proof: measured 2026-10-29 on p13: PostgreSQL 17.5 (the port's tarball), --enable-debug CFLAGS='-O1 -g' CPPFLAGS=-DUSE_VALGRIND (no cassert, as the port), test_decoding installed, trigger.sql's statements through `postgres --single -c wal_level=logical` under Valgrind 3.26 with src/tools/valgrind.supp: one error, 'Invalid read of size 8' at ReorderBufferProcessTXN (reorderbuffer.c:2501) by ReorderBufferReplay by ReorderBufferCommit by DecodeCommit ... by pg_logical_slot_get_changes; the address is inside an 8192-byte block from SlabAllocFromNewBlock, allocated by ReorderBufferGetChange. control.sql (99 rows): no error. 97 rows: no error either, as the threshold arithmetic predicts. Natively the stale read is silent and decoding returns its 101 rows.
fidelity: real server, core. Upstream reproduced it with CHANGES_THRESHOLD recompiled to 1; this trigger reaches the same read in the release as shipped by sizing the transaction so the hundredth change is the freed one. The same defect is ../../mmgr-repros/04_9e0b4b1ab5_reorderbuffer_spec_insert_lsn as a C program against the real Slab context; not two defects.
nested_why: the freed change is a Slab chunk inside an 8 KiB block the Change context keeps; malloc never sees it freed
fault_sites_why: Valgrind with PostgreSQL's own mempool annotations (USE_VALGRIND) on the host, recorded before any Capstone arm ran: the invalid read is at ReorderBufferProcessTXN (reorderbuffer.c:2501), the update_progress_txn call's change->lsn. A fault elsewhere counts through control.sql.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, PostgreSQL's contexts stock (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng): a fault after the trigger started that its control.sql or a justified fault_sites ties to the defect, or the trigger completes and this arm did not see it

virtual-pg-pools.oracle: virtual profile with the memory-context port's patch 0003: every palloc chunk a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), revoked by pfree and repalloc (CREVOKE) (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng-pg-pools): as virtual-malloc

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes: the change is freed into its Slab block, which libc's revocation never sees freed, so the platform has nothing to revoke

status: live at the pin, measured on the host under Valgrind (2026-10-29); no Capstone or CheriBSD arm has run it
